title: Jharkhand CM Soren Breaks Silence on Recruitment Row as Protests Escalate
excerpt: Hemant Soren promises 'decisions at appropriate time' as thousands of job aspirants stage indefinite protests in Ranchi over alleged irregularities in JPSC and JSSC examinations.
body:
• Jharkhand CM Hemant Soren broke his silence on the recruitment exam controversy, saying decisions would be taken "at the appropriate time."
  • Thousands of aspirants have launched an indefinite sit-in at Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium in Ranchi, demanding a CBI probe into JPSC and JSSC exam irregularities.
  • The state CID investigation has made several arrests, but protesters and the BJP opposition reject it as inadequate and demand a central agency inquiry.
  • Former CM Raghubar Das has called for dialogue with aspirants and urged the government to hand the probe to the CBI.

Jharkhand Chief Minister Hemant Soren has broken weeks of silence on the growing recruitment examination controversy that has brought thousands of job aspirants onto the streets of Ranchi, saying his government would take "decisions at the appropriate time" on the matter.

Soren's remarks came as an indefinite sit-in protest by aspirants at Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium entered its second week, with demonstrators demanding an independent probe into alleged irregularities in examinations conducted by the Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) and the Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission (JSSC).

Protests Intensify Across Ranchi

On July 29, thousands of aspirants organised a 'Constitution March' from Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium to Albert Ekka Chowk, drawing participants from districts across the state, according to IANS. The march saw large-scale participation despite intermittent rain, with demonstrators carrying banners reading "Stop playing with the future of JPSC aspirants," "Fix accountability in JPSC and JSSC," and "Hemant Soren, resign."

https://x.com/dna/status/2084671173317754948

The protesters warned that if the government fails to act on their demands, they would convert the stadium into a permanent protest site on the lines of Delhi's Jantar Mantar. Hundreds of candidates began an indefinite dharna at the stadium, with the movement being intensified in phases.

"If the government does not take positive steps, we will turn this stadium into a permanent protest venue."

— Protesting aspirants at Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium, Ranchi

The agitation disrupted traffic across several key roads in Ranchi. Long queues of vehicles stretched from Kachahari Chowk to Albert Ekka Chowk, with congestion spilling over to Main Road, Radium Road and Lalpur Road for hours, according to reports.

BJP Clashes and Political Fallout

The recruitment row has also drawn sharp political confrontation. On July 22, the BJP's youth wing protested outside the JPSC office, demanding the cancellation of the 14th Combined Civil Services Preliminary Examination over alleged irregularities. Clashes broke out after protesters tried to breach barricades and march towards the Commission's office. The BJP alleged that results had been declared without publishing cut-off marks.

Former Chief Minister and BJP leader Raghubar Das has urged the Soren government to engage in dialogue with the protesting aspirants and hand the investigation to the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), calling the ongoing state CID probe insufficient.

The aspirants' demands centre on allegations of paper leaks, manipulation in the recruitment process, and irregularities in the excise constable recruitment. Several YouTube channels and social media posts have amplified the movement, describing it as one of the largest Gen Z-led youth protests in the state's history.

CID Probe and Government's Defence

The state government has maintained that the CID investigation is progressing, with several arrests already made in connection with the alleged irregularities. Earlier, the Jharkhand High Court had rejected a petition seeking a CBI probe into the JSSC Combined Graduate Level examination, directing the commission to declare results and proceed with recruitment.

Soren had previously accused the BJP of orchestrating a conspiracy around the JSSC-CGL exams to undermine the state's youth. In December 2025, while distributing appointment letters to 1,910 successful candidates, the chief minister said the opposition was willing to "jeopardise the dreams of countless young people" for political gain.

"A conspiracy can indeed blur the truth for a short while, but it can never erase it."

— Hemant Soren, Chief Minister of Jharkhand

Government ministers have pointed to over 34,000 appointments made through the JSSC and 3,000 through the JPSC between 2020 and 2025 as evidence of the administration's commitment to recruitment, calling it unprecedented since Jharkhand's creation as a state.

What's Next

The standoff shows no signs of easing. Protesters have vowed to escalate their agitation if the government does not address their demands for transparency and accountability in the recruitment process. The BJP has signalled it will continue to press for a CBI inquiry and keep the recruitment row at the centre of its campaign against the Soren government.

With Jharkhand's politically sensitive tribal belt watching closely, the recruitment controversy threatens to erode Soren's support among the state's youth — a demographic that proved decisive in the 2024 assembly elections that returned the JMM-led alliance to power. How the chief minister navigates the crisis in the coming weeks could shape the political landscape ahead of future electoral battles.
nri_angle: The recruitment exam controversy in Jharkhand highlights systemic challenges in India's public employment processes, a concern for diaspora families whose relatives depend on government job prospects.
